spec.description: Find places by name and return their coordinates, time zone and administrative context.

name.description: Place name to search for. Two characters match exactly; three or more match by prefix, fuzzily.

language.description: Two-letter language code for the returned names; falls back to English.

format.description: Response format. Only JSON is representable by this client; the API also serves protobuf.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code to restrict results to one country.

response.title: SearchResults
response.description: The matching places, best match first. `results` is absent when nothing matched.

items.title: Place
items.description: One place from the GeoNames-based index.

name.description: Place name in the requested language.

feature_code.description: GeoNames feature code, such as `PPLC` for a capital.

admin1_id.description: Id of the first-level administrative area.

admin2_id.description: Id of the second-level administrative area.

admin3_id.description: Id of the third-level administrative area.

admin4_id.description: Id of the fourth-level administrative area.

admin1.description: First-level administrative area, such as a state.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of the place.

generationtime_ms.description: Server time spent generating the response, in milliseconds.

unverified.detail: No recording yet: the sandbox this spec was written in cannot reach open-meteo.com. The `record.yml` workflow replays `examples/*.request.json` through the generated client with `truewire capture` and opens a pull request with the responses.

notes: The `format` enum lists only `json`: the API also answers `protobuf`, which a JSON-validating client cannot represent, so the value is left out rather than typed as accepted and then rejected at validation.
Administrative fields and `country_code` are optional: the index has places, oceans among them, without them.
`apikey` is redacted because the transport adds it to the query on the commercial tier; the free tier sends none.
